classes.name: Oral atypical antipsychotics
classes.description: Second-generation oral antipsychotics: aripiprazole, quetiapine IR/ER, olanzapine, risperidone, ziprasidone, lurasidone (Latuda), paliperidone ER, cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, iloperidone, clozapine, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi).
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or add-on treatment for depression.

classes.name: Long-acting injectable antipsychotics
classes.description: Long-acting injectables: aripiprazole (Abilify Maintena, Abilify Asimtufii, Aristada), paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna/Trinza/Hafyera), risperidone (Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Rykindo), olanzapine pamoate (Zyprexa Relprevv), haloperidol and fluphenazine decanoate.
classes.plainDescription: A shot every few weeks or months instead of a daily pill.

preferredAgent.sig: Schizophrenia: start 2 mg/day (1 mg twice daily or 2 mg once), titrate by 1-2 mg/day to 4-8 mg/day. Bipolar mania: 2-3 mg once daily. Dose per indication (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A pill once or twice a day; your prescriber adjusts the dose.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.16 (Central Nervous System, Antipsychotics, Oral: Atypical & Misc.) directly. Preferred column lists 9 agents with no PA; PA column lists 28 agents, all brand or specific-form items. Judgment call: risperidone tablet chosen as a preferred generic commonly written for schizophrenia; aripiprazole, olanzapine, quetiapine and lurasidone are equally preferred. Strength and sig are standard label starting dose, not printed on the PDL. No quantity limit printed for this class. Haloperidol, fluphenazine and other conventional antipsychotics are not listed on the PDL; this heading is not stated as a complete list, so their absence is not an exclusion.

preferredAgent.sig: 25 mg IM every 2 weeks. Continue oral risperidone (or another oral antipsychotic) for 3 weeks after the first injection, because drug release is delayed. Establish tolerability with oral risperidone first (label).
preferredAgent.sigShort: 25 mg IM q2wk + oral x3 wk
preferredAgent.plainSig: A shot every 2 weeks; keep taking your pills for the first 3 weeks.

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p.16 (Antipsychotics, Long-Acting Injectables). The class is marked '* Clinical criteria may apply' and links the DC injectable atypical antipsychotic PA form; recorded as a restriction on the pick, not as PA. The PDL states HCP-administered drugs are generally not included, yet these injectables are listed, so the benefit (pharmacy vs medical) is not stated. Judgment call: Risperdal Consta chosen among 8 preferred LAIs as a widely used agent with a non-branded risperidone base; Abilify Maintena is an equally defensible pick. Haloperidol decanoate and fluphenazine decanoate do not appear; not a stated exclusion.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp. 66, 71-73 (Atypical Antipsychotics and Antimanic sections). Aripiprazole 5 mg tablet is F with QL 60/30 days and AL min 6 years (p. 71); the tablet strength is printed as a list, so 5 mg is the lowest listed strength and is a judgment call on the preferred pick. Not on the list: lurasidone (Latuda), cariprazine (Vraylar), brexpiprazole (Rexulti), lumateperone (Caplyta), asenapine, paliperidone oral, olanzapine/samidorphan (Lybalvi). The document does not state that the list is complete, so these are absent from coverage, not recorded as excluded.

Not on the list: Risperdal Consta (brand). Doses and sigs are standard label dosing, not printed in the document.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp.72-76 (formulary pp.70-74). Preferred aripiprazole 10 mg tablet is Tier 1 with no flag. All generic oral atypicals on the list are Tier 1 with no flag. Vraylar is Tier 2 with ST; PA**. Not listed in this document: brand-only Abilify, Seroquel, Geodon, Latuda, Caplyta, Rexulti, Lybalvi, Fanapt. The document does not say it is a complete list, so these are not recorded as nonformulary. Cobenfy (Tier 3, no flag, PDF p.73) is outside this class description and not recorded. Pick is a judgment call: aripiprazole chosen as a common once-daily Tier 1 generic.

records.verificationNote: Read PDF pp.72-76. Haloperidol decanoate 100 mg/mL and fluphenazine decanoate 25 mg/mL are Tier 1 with no flag. Invega Sustenna, Trinza, Hafyera, Aristada, Erzofri and Rykindo are Tier 2 with no flag. No LAI carries PA or ST here. Not listed in this document: Abilify Maintena, Risperdal Consta, Perseris, Uzedy, Zyprexa Relprevv. These are likely provider-administered (medical benefit) products, so their absence is not treated as nonformulary. Marked partial because the benefit routing is not printed. Pick is a judgment call: lowest-tier Tier 1 generic decanoate; the document prints no dose, so the sig states label dosing without a number.
